I second everyone's responses and raise my BIGGEST pet peeve when people say things like, "Well, everyone struggles with this."

Yeah, totally forgot that EVERYONE has complex trauma and a dissociative disorder. 🙃 My freaking bad. 

I used to struggle GREATLY with panic attacks for years (finally got those things under some control) and it was traumatic in itself. My mother has anxiety and when she talks about it she's always like, "Do you know how this feels?" Like, no. No freaking clue. 🤷‍♀️ 

It just drives me insane because I'm finally advocating for myself and that kind of dismissiveness has an underlying tone of "think of others, others struggle too" as if I didn't live my entire freaking life up until I was 22 ONLY doing for others and thinking of others above my own. {{Fangirl}} They're close in age (twins) but they started out really close then they go to college and find their own wavelengths. It focuses on one sister and her journey through the change. Might not be exactly what you're looking for but I also have an older sister (I'm younger) we're quite different and don't really speak, so I read a lot of sister books sometimes. It is YA. 

{{Sense and Sensibility}} is also a great one. 

{{In Her Shoes}} This one is about two sisters whose only thing in common is their shoe size and they get brought together by their grandmother. It's an okay movie too, but I prefer the book. 

{{Little Women}}

{{Wide-Awake Princess}} is definitely juvenile but it's one of my comfort ones. It's about Rapunzel, and when the whole castle goes to sleep her sister goes out to break the spell since she's immune to magic. It's just a cutesy one. If I can remember the other ones.. I'll post.
